title: Merapi Run 2026 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: Merapi Run 2026 Review: Kaliurang Hills, Cool Air, Finish Times
meta_description: Merapi Run 2026 review: a 493 m-climb half marathon from Kaliurang, 15°C at the 5am start, eight water stations, a four-hour cut-off and how fast the field ran.
dek: What the 9 August 2026 race on Merapi's lower slopes was like: the climbs, the cool air at the 5am start, aid stations and cut-offs, roads shared with traffic, and how fast the half-marathon and 10 km fields ran.
verdict: Enter if you want a hilly half marathon or 10 km in cool mountain air rather than a fast time. The 2026 race started and finished at a hotel in Kaliurang, about 900 m up the slopes of Mount Merapi, with 493 m of climbing on the half and 238 m on the 10 km. It was about 15°C at the 5am start, cold by Indonesian standards, and still only about 21°C at the 9am half-marathon cut-off. The limits are generous: four hours for the half and three for the 10 km, and no timed finisher was outside them. Expect slow times: the median half marathoner took 2:36, and the roads are open to traffic.

sections.heading: The Course: Up and Down Merapi's Lower Slopes
paragraphs: All four distances start and finish at the Griya Persada Convention Hotel & Resort in Kaliurang, the hill resort north of Yogyakarta on the southern slope of Mount Merapi [1][2]. The organiser puts the climbing at 493 m for the half marathon, 238 m for the 10 km, 142 m for the 5 km and 98 m for the 3 km family run [1]. Because the start and finish are the same point, every metre climbed is also descended.

The roads are a mix of asphalt and concrete, and GPX files of each route were published for download [2]. The half marathon is still new: it was added in 2025, with a new route from Griya Persada, for what was then the race's fifth edition since 2019 [3].

The race used to start elsewhere in Kaliurang. In 2022, when the 10 km started and finished at Suraloka Zoo, one runner described a steep 2 km descent at the start, about 6 km of climbing, and a 2 km descent to the finish, with a timing checkpoint at Telogo Putri [4]. The route has changed since, but the pattern of long climbs on Merapi's foothills, at roughly 600 m to 1,000 m, has not.

sections.heading: The Weather: Cool, Damp Mountain Air
paragraphs: Open-Meteo's historical model for the start area, at 899 m, gives 15°C at 5am on race morning, with a dew point of 15°C, 99% humidity and an 8 km/h breeze [5]. The air was saturated but cool. It warmed slowly: 16°C at 6am, 18°C at 7am, 19°C at 8am and 21°C with 77% humidity at 9am, when the half marathon closed [5]. No rain fell in the model during the race.

These are modelled figures for the hillside, not airport readings; the nearest airports are in the lowlands, where it is much warmer. For lowland Java runners this is one of the few races where heat is not the main problem. The climbing is.

sections.heading: Aid Stations and Cut-offs
paragraphs: The half marathon had eight water stations and three fruit stations, the 10 km three water stations and one fruit station, and the 5 km one water station, serving mineral water and an isotonic drink; food was at the finish only [2]. The 3 km family run had no water station [2].

Start times in 2026 were 5am for the half marathon, 5.30am for the 10 km, 5.45am for the 5 km and 6am for the 3 km, with cut-offs of four hours, three hours, two hours and an hour and a half [2]. Runners were asked to be at the start 30 minutes early, and anyone more than five minutes late was moved to the next category's start [2].
The limits are loose for the field. The slowest timed half-marathon finisher took 3:57:44 and the slowest 10 km finisher 2:27:28, both inside the limit [6].

sections.heading: The Roads: Open to Traffic
paragraphs: The course is not closed. The organiser's terms say the route is shared with other road users, with marshals posted along it, and that the route can change with notice on the website or social media [2]. Entrants accept the accident risk of a road race, and the organiser said it had arranged insurance [2]. On the steep descents, stay alert for vehicles coming up behind you as well as ahead.

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The official results list 183 half-marathon and 264 10 km finishers; the 5 km and 3 km are not included [6].

The half marathon was won in 1:18:15, and the top ten ran between 1:18 and 1:47. The median finisher took 2:36:25; only 9% broke two hours, 42% broke two and a half, and 90% were done by 3:14:24. Women made up 20% of finishers, and the fastest woman ran 1:35:32 [6].
In the 10 km the top ten ran 36:16 to 52:08, the median was 1:20:14, 8% broke an hour and 90% were done by 1:44:01. Women were 29% of 10 km finishers [6].

Those times are slow for the distances, which is the climbing showing through: a runner who goes under two hours here would be inside the top 10% of the half-marathon field. With a field this size, a top-ten place needs a sub-1:47 half or a 52-minute 10 km.

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Race packs were collected on Saturday 8 August, 10am to 9pm, at the Pendopo Maliawan in the Griya Persada hotel, with the confirmation email and original ID; one person could collect for up to five runners with a signed authorisation [2]. Every finisher got a medal and an e-certificate, and half marathoners also got a finisher jersey [2].

Entry cost Rp500,000 for the half marathon, Rp350,000 for the 10 km, Rp250,000 for the 5 km and Rp200,000 for the 3 km [1]. Entries cannot be refunded or transferred to another runner, even if the race is cancelled for reasons beyond the organiser's control [2].
For a 5am start on a hillside north of Yogyakarta, staying at the race hotel or elsewhere in Kaliurang the night before is the simplest option.

sections.heading: Should You Enter the Next Merapi Run?
paragraphs: Yes, if you enjoy hills, want to race in cool air for once, or want a first half marathon with a generous four-hour limit: the slowest finisher in 2026 still made it inside the cut-off. It suits a holiday in Yogyakarta, with the race hotel as the race centre.
Think twice if you want a fast time or closed roads. The median half took 2:36, and the course is shared with traffic.
This review draws on the organiser's race information and terms, local reporting on the 2025 race, one runner's account of the 2022 race, modelled weather data and the official results.

faqs.question: How hilly is the Merapi Run?
faqs.answer: Very. The organiser puts the climbing at 493 m for the half marathon and 238 m for the 10 km, on roads around Kaliurang at roughly 900 m on Mount Merapi's southern slope. Start and finish are at the same hotel, so you descend as much as you climb. The median half marathoner took 2:36 in 2026.

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times at the Merapi Run?
faqs.answer: In 2026 the limits were four hours for the half marathon, three hours for the 10 km, two hours for the 5 km and an hour and a half for the 3 km family run. They are generous: the slowest timed half-marathon finisher took 3:57 and the slowest 10 km finisher 2:27, both inside the limit.

faqs.question: What is the weather like at the Merapi Run?
faqs.answer: Cool for Indonesia. At the 5am start on 9 August 2026, Open-Meteo's historical model for Kaliurang gives 15°C with 99% humidity and a light breeze, rising to about 21°C by the 9am half-marathon cut-off. Expect cool, saturated air rather than heat; no rain fell during the race.

faqs.question: What time does the Merapi Run start?
faqs.answer: In 2026 the half marathon started at 5am, the 10 km at 5.30am, the 5 km at 5.45am and the 3 km family run at 6am, all from the Griya Persada hotel in Kaliurang. Runners had to be at the start 30 minutes early; anyone more than five minutes late was moved to the next category's start.

editorial_notes: Reinstated 2026-11-06: withdrawn 2026-09-28 because no report of any edition could be found; official results for the 9 August 2026 race (PickMyRace event record dated 9 August 2026) now confirm it ran, and this review covers that edition.
